sections.overview: This small beetle is a widespread pest of stored foods.
sections.identification: Adults are reddish brown and about 2–4 mm long.
sections.habitat: It is often found in homes, shops, warehouses and kitchens where dry foods are stored.
sections.diet: Larvae feed on dry foods, including flour, biscuits and spices.
sections.behavior: Larvae tunnel through food and can reach supplies hidden inside packaging.
sections.reproduction: It develops through egg, larva, pupa and adult stages; females lay eggs on or near a food source.
sections.ecology: Development speed depends on temperature, moisture and food quality.
sections.conservation: The references consulted describe it as a stored-food pest rather than provide a conservation assessment.
